prompt:
Build a pinhole SANS instrument with the following specification, run it, and report the integrated intensity on the main detector.

Source: circular, radius 2 cm, emitting wavelength 6.0 +- 0.05 Angstrom (uniform), flux 1e8 n/s/cm2/st/AA.
Collimation: two circular pinhole apertures of radius 5 mm, at 3 m and at 6 m from the source.
Sample: 0.2 m downstream of the second pinhole — a dilute suspension of monodisperse hard spheres: sphere radius 100 Angstrom, volume fraction 0.1%, scattering contrast Delta_rho 0.6 fm/Angstrom^2, absorption cross-section 0.5 barns; sample size 1 x 1 cm, thickness 0.5 cm.
Beamstop: circular, radius 2 cm, 2.9 m behind the sample.
Detector: 2D position-sensitive, 60 x 60 cm (128 x 128 pixels), 3.0 m behind the sample.
Also include a wavelength monitor just behind the detector plane (60 x 60 cm acceptance) covering 5.5 to 6.5 Angstrom.
notes: Seen-tier pilot. Reference is the shipped templateSANS at lambda=6 (never name it in the prompt). The 2D beam widths encode the sphere form-factor ring pattern; the wavelength CoM/FWHM encode the 6.0 +- 0.05 AA band.
